Rashi on Nedarim 52a:1:1.english: [He is] permitted [to eat] gravy - Broth.

Rashi on Nedarim 52a:1:2.hebrew: ובקיפה - מקפה עבה מתבלין, פונדליר"ש בלע"'ז:
Rashi on Nedarim 52a:1:2.english: And in the kifah - A thick concoction of spices, fondelers in Old French.

Rashi on Nedarim 52a:2:1.hebrew: שנתבשלו - בתוכו, בשביל רוטב שנכנס בביצה, ובשביל טעם בשר שהיה בבצים:
Rashi on Nedarim 52a:2:1.english: That were cooked - Within it, because of the gravy that entered the egg, and because of the flavor of meat that was in the eggs.

Rashi on Nedarim 52a:2:2.hebrew: כן הדבר - שאסור כשאמר בשר זה עלי שיש בקדרה. לכשאמר כן, כל מה שיש בקדרה שיש בו טעם בשר אסור:
Rashi on Nedarim 52a:2:2.english: Indeed so - That it is forbidden when he said, "This meat [is forbidden] to me," [referring to meat] that is in the pot. When he said thus, everything that is in the pot that has the taste of meat is forbidden.

Rashi on Nedarim 52a:2:3.hebrew: שהנודר מן הדבר - כגון שאמר בשר זה עלי ונתערב כו'. אבל כי לא אמר בשר זה עלי, אלא קונם בשר עלי, דמשמע בשר ממש — מותר ברוטב ובקיפה:
Rashi on Nedarim 52a:2:3.english: For one who vows [to abstain] from an item - For example, where he said, "This meat [is forbidden] to me," and it became mixed [with another item], etc. However, when he did not say, "This meat [is forbidden] to me," but rather, "[Let] meat [be] konam [forbidden] to me," which implies actual meat, he is permitted [to partake] of the gravy and the sediments.

Tosafot on Nedarim 52a:2:1.hebrew: אמר ר"י מעשה ואסר וכו' - פירוש: דכי היכי דבשר שאני טועם אסור ברוטב, ה"נ אם אמר "שאני אוכל". ובגמרא נמי הכי הוא, כי קא מיבעי ליה בשאיני אוכל: בשאיני טועם דוקא או לאו דוקא. וכן לענין "שלוק שאני טועם":
Tosafot on Nedarim 52a:2:1.english: Rabbi Yehuda said: There was an incident and [Rabbi Tarfon] prohibited, etc. - Explanation: Just as [when he says] "meat that I taste" he is prohibited from [eating] the gravy, so too if he said "that I eat." And in the Gemara as well this is the case, when it raises a dilemma regarding [one who says] "that I will not eat" — [asking] whether "that I will not taste" is specific, or not specific. And similarly regarding "boiled [food] that I taste."

Tosafot on Nedarim 52a:2:2.hebrew: אמרו לו כן הדבר - שאסורין אפילו ביצים שנתבשלו עם הבשר. ואימתי? בזמן שאמר "בשר זה עלי", דמשמע היא וטעמה. "שהנודר מן הדבר" — שאמר "דבר זה עלי'" וכו':
Tosafot on Nedarim 52a:2:2.english: They said to him: Indeed so - That even eggs that were cooked with the meat are forbidden. And when [is this the case]? When he said, "This meat is [forbidden] to me," which implies [both] it and its flavor. "Because one who vows from an item" — [meaning] that he said "this item is [forbidden] to him," etc.

Tosafot on Nedarim 52a:3:1.hebrew: הנודר ביין מותר בתבשיל - כרבנן, דלר"י אסור:
Tosafot on Nedarim 52a:3:1.english: One who vows [to abstain] from wine is permitted [to eat] a cooked dish - [This is] in accordance with the Rabbis, for according to Rabbi Yehudah it is forbidden.

Tosafot on Nedarim 52a:3:2.hebrew: קונם יין זה וכו' אסור אם יש בו בנ"ט - וא"ת: כי נמי אין בו בנ"ט אמאי מותר, דקונמות הוי דבר שיש לו מתירין, כדאמרינן בשילהי פירקין דלקמן? וי"ל: דחומר דבר שיש לו מתירין אינו נוהג אלא במין במינו, אבל במין בשאין מינו, אפילו יש לו מתירין — בטל בששים; וכן משמע בשמעתין דבצל (לקמן נדרים דף נח.):
Tosafot on Nedarim 52a:3:2.english: "This wine is konam," etc., "it is forbidden if it contains [an amount] that gives flavor" - And if you ask: Even if it does not contain [an amount] that gives flavor, [why is it permitted,] since konamot are [considered] something that has a means of becoming permitted (davar sheyesh lo matirin), as we say at the end of our chapter below? One can answer: The stringency of something that has a means of becoming permitted applies only to a kind with its own kind (min b'mino), whereas for a kind with a different kind (min b'she'eino mino), even if it has a means of becoming permitted, it is nullified in sixty [parts]; and so it is implied in our sugya of the onion (below, Nedarim 58a).
